mechanism.lock_file_metadata: pid, host, uuid and acquired_at fields compatible with zcp_test.gpu.gpu_lock_status; cleared in place before unlock
mechanism.lease_metadata_role: owner, heartbeat, lease and command observability only
mechanism.expired_lease_behavior: never unlink or otherwise bypass a kernel-held lock
mechanism.fd_scope: the lock wrapper only; heartbeat and task subprocesses explicitly close the descriptor before execution
mechanism.release_boundary: immediately after the task subprocess exits, independently of the outer supervisor lifetime
mechanism.cleanup: lease-matched metadata is removed on success, task failure, INT and TERM

verified_invariants: The lock-file inode remains unchanged across acquisition, timeout, release and reacquisition.
While held, the lock file exposes pid, host, uuid and Beijing acquired_at owner metadata; release truncates this metadata without unlinking the inode.
A task subprocess has no file descriptor referencing the GPU lock path.
The kernel lock is reacquirable while the outer supervisor remains alive after its task finishes.
Heartbeat updates preserve the same lease ID and owner PID.
A timed-out contender neither replaces active owner metadata nor removes the lock file.
TERM returns 143, terminates the task, removes matching metadata and releases flock.
A task exit status of 7 is propagated after metadata cleanup and flock release.
Invalid lease configuration fails before acquiring a lock.
limitations: SIGKILL cannot run shell metadata cleanup; kernel flock still releases automatically, and a later real acquirer atomically replaces stale observability metadata.
Lease expiry is intentionally not an unlock mechanism.

Single-GPU ImageNet candidate and DARTS resume launchers reacquire the shared task-scoped wrapper for every serial scientific task; concurrent AutoFormer search groups retain a lock only while their active searches run. The all-GPU DDP path retains atomic multi-lock acquisition for one active DDP task and releases all descriptors when that task exits.

Acceptance jobs launched from older immutable source snapshots retain their snapshotted lock implementation until they finish; they are audited through kernel flock and active child/GPU PID checks rather than modified in place.
